title: Regional response to proposed provincial planning changes
subtitle: Also: Stage 2 ION options, Bill 5 endorsement, student housing purchase, speed cameras and a statement against hate.
overview: Regional Council approved the Region's response to the province's proposed new Provincial Planning Statement {{vote:m12}}. Delegates warned that allowing farm severances and rural residential lots would harm farmland and environmentally sensitive areas. Council directed the Regional Chair to advocate with the province and agreed individual councillors should also write to it.

Council directed staff to widen the Stage 2 ION business case with extra alternatives, emergency ramps and bus rapid transit costing {{vote:m11}}. It also approved buying a 88-unit student residence at 139 University Avenue West for $11,250,000 to add to housing supply, and a property at 1650 Dundas Street South in Cambridge. Other approvals included faster speed-camera expansion to 32 sites, a LED traffic signal tender, a multi-year accessibility plan and an endorsement of Bill 5 on removing councillors who breach harassment policies.

After a delegation on transphobia in Norwich Township, Council passed a resolution opposing hate and prejudice and urging other municipalities to do the same. Reports on encampments and supports for Council were received for information.

decisions.detail: Council forwarded the staff report to the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing as the Region's response to the proposed new Provincial Planning Statement.

Council directed staff to include three project alternatives plus emergency ramps, a Cambridge-to-Preston alternative, an east Cambridge terminus option, a Dundas route feasibility review, and costed bus rapid transit.

decisions.item: Student residence and Cambridge property purchases
decisions.detail: Council authorized buying 139 University Avenue West for $11,250,000, funded by reserves, COVID recovery funds and debentures, with one new maintenance position, and buying 1650 Dundas Street South for $1,300,000.

decisions.item: Speed cameras, New Dundee water and route 2 bus
decisions.detail: Council advanced funding and a staff hire to reach 32 automated speed enforcement sites, accepted the New Dundee water treatment assessment, and asked staff to report in June on options to offset closing GRT routes 2 and 73.
Council endorsed Bill 5, which would let councils seek removal of members who violate workplace harassment policies, and directed an amendment to the procedure by-law to record all votes in minutes.
Council approved the Multi-Year Accessibility Plan 2023-2027.
Council accepted Fortran Traffic Systems' tender of $1,483,695.20 over three years and added $1,080,100 to the 2024 and 2025 capital budget from the Transportation Capital Reserve.
Council declared opposition to hate, racism and discrimination, including against 2SLGBTQIA+ people and persons with disabilities, and will send it to area municipalities and AMO.

debate: Delegates argued the proposed planning changes are not needed to address the housing shortage. They said there is enough land inside urban boundaries and that the changes would remove local discretion over rural lot creation.

A delegate from the agricultural community said allowing three severances per farm parcel would fragment farmland, create conflicts with neighbouring residential lots and make it hard to build or expand livestock operations. They estimated up to 8000 acres could be lost in the Region.

Another delegate said multi-lot rural development on private septics and wells could affect environmentally sensitive landscapes, and that lots would likely be large because of servicing needs. Delegates urged councillors to write personally to the Premier.

During discussion, one councillor said political advocacy should supplement staff's technical response, with a nuanced position that some severances may work. The Chair confirmed they would carry Council's support to the province.

On supports for Council, councillors said directly elected members face growing demands in a part-time role, but cautioned against assigning a staff member to every councillor. Staff said all regional staff serve all councillors, and councillors expected to return to the policy question.
On the anti-hate motion, councillors added persons with disabilities, reordered the wording to equity, diversity and inclusion, and added encouragement for other municipalities to take a stand.
